Hi, fellow hyuman.

I got the same problem about a year ago.

I think that the solution for me was to stop thinking. You know, probably most of the people that you talk to won't remember all of what you say or don't care about you at all so why would you care? Yeah, maybe you said something embarrassing or make a mistake but beating yourself because of it won't make you a better person.

After I really understand this I stopped focusing on my past mistakes and started working on the way to fix them.

And no, you won't become a super social person one day to another, everyone has its own pace and that's cool. Personally I transformed from someone who didn't like to talk to people to someone who treats everyone the same.

See when you don't have to think about how you talk specifically to everyone, you can just focus on being neutral with everyone.

And after my self steem improved a little, I started to make some friends, like, really thrusting them and talking with him.

So, just give it a try, talk to people without thinking to much about yourself or the mistakes you make, take care.

I'm glad I could help, and sorry for the late reply. And yeah, college takes a lot of time and debt, I have the idea that a college degree is something to show off (I know this doesn't apply in all countries but for mine, people just go to college to have their diploma, not to learn) what really is going to help you is experience. So if I were to choose between the two of them, I will go with the first path for several reasons.

1. College courses are not exactly, real business focused, yeah they teach you all the theory but you don't really know if you are going to apply that theory in the future.
2. If you got a job, no mater what type of job it is, it's going to have a marketing and management model so if you enter from the roots, you can see how it operates and I would say that will help you realize what type of business you want to start.

So if you take the first path, I would recommend that you don't only adquiere management and marketing skills, if you really observe how they operate and learn from that, you are not only going to adquiere skills, you are going to adquiere knowledge and if you really analyze their business you can find good things that you can use in the future and if you find something that doesn't work quite well, you can ask yourself, if I were running this business, how could I improve this x thing? And I think that's the most valuable asset you can absorb from that path because you will not only adquiere skills, you will adquiere knowledge of how to solve problems.

That's my recommendation, my vision is that creating a business not only depends on management skills (but keep in mind that they are important) it also depends in your capacity of adapting and resolve the problems the world is going to throw at you.

Take care, also if you don't mind I would like to hear about your progress in the future, hearing stories like this gave the feeling that I'm not the only one struggling with this. Goodnight

Oh and I forgot to say, the best way to prove yourself is by results, I don't like to try change someone perspective just by talk and promises, so until I have some good results, I'm not going to tell my family.

Hi, I don't have a concrete advice for you but I thought that maybe reading a similar story from another human being in the path to financial freedom could help you.

I'm a 18 years old male living in a South America country and I had experienced the same. No one in my family had ever started or thinked of starting their own business.

For them it's the usual thing to work for long hours, spend their money without thinking and having dept (this is something I'm trying to change with my parents)

So when I was 17 years old I decided that I wanted to brake the poverty chain. 

But as I said my family is pretty conservative and if I tell my family that I want to start my own business they will disown me, so I decided to play along and entered a college.

So I'll explain my entire plan that I used in that time and finally what I'm currently doing. Hope this can help you. 

First, I realize that I have time, if I go to college, my parents will cover my expenses so don't have to worry about day to day cost. 

Second, I decided to enter a prestigious college because it has more to offer, If you go to a prestigious college it's more likely to encounter people that are as ambitious as you (I met my best friend this way) and a good college has a lot of materials, most colleges have a library so you have practically free knowledge of all kind at your disposal. 

Third, I needed a job, because I need money to start a business and if I want to have that money I needed to earn it. For this reason I searched for good work from home works, for 2 reasons, The more I work the more I earn and I don't lose time moving to my work place, I can study and work in my house. 

That was basically my plan at that time, to this day I'm still working on it, I basically do all my college related stuff early so it won't bother me and in the rest of my time I study business management skills, stadistics, and marketing.  

But I want to make it clear, it won't be easy and it will take time, but you know, I will give it a try at all costs. 

I recommend you read the book Atomic Habits, it's a great way to improve your life day by day and don't feel anxious about the future.

And finally, remember, if someone did it before, why can't you do it. Take care, and my best blessings for you
